title: stateful constraint router: unified CFG + regex backends with tokenizer adjacency adaptor
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Streaming structured outputs (tool calls, JSON schemas, CSV fragments) showed intermittent corruption when constraints spanned chunk boundaries. Existing backends treat constraints statelessly which leads to regex anchors or CFG nonterminals being applied without knowledge of prior partial tokens from previous stream frames. This PR introduces a stateful constraint router that unifies CFG and regex backends and layers a tokenizer adjacency adaptor to preserve subtoken boundaries across stream frames.

What this does: Adds a routing layer that tracks partial match context per-request and dispatches token candidates to either CFG or regex engines based on parse state and heuristic priority. The tokenizer adjacency adaptor records the right/left subtoken fragments for the last emitted token and rehydrates them into the constraint engines on the next frame so anchors and lookbehinds operate on proper grapheme/subtoken boundaries.

Key changes (single-string summary):
- core/constraints/router.rs: new stateful router with per-request ConstraintContext and a priority table for backend selection based on parse depth, regex complexity, and streaming-latency hints.
- core/constraints/cfg_backend.rs: CFG backend extended with incremental parse state that accepts fragmentary tokens and exposes suspend/resume points.
- core/constraints/regex_backend.rs: Regex backend gains a small DFA cache keyed by adjacency signature and supports anchored partial-match continuation.
- core/tokenizer/adaptor.rs: TokenizerAdjacencyAdaptor tracks subtoken suffix/prefix fragments and provides a minimal normalization to avoid accidental merge/split when applying constraints.
- api/compat/openai_streaming_shim.rs: Updates to emit function-call framing boundaries in a way compatible with the new router so tool-calls don't get split mid-argument structure.
- runtime/tests/constraint_stream_integration.rs: New integration harness that replays sampled production traces with artificial frame sizes and verifies structural invariants across stream boundaries.
- docs/notes/constraint-router.md: Design doc describing heuristics and operational knobs (priority table, fragment retention TTL).

Backward compatibility: The router defaults to legacy stateless mode for existing customers; enabling stateful routing requires setting the new inference config flag constraints.router=stateful in dedicated/private deployments or via experimental feature flag in hosted. This makes the change opt-in while we monitor telemetry.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests cover CFG incremental parse correctness and DFA continuation semantics.
- Integration tests run a fuzz harness on sampled streaming chunk sizes (1-64 bytes) against known-good structured outputs from the eval corpus.
- A mini canary run was executed on staging with subset customers; we validated zero increase in 99th percentile token latency and eliminated 95% of previously observed structure-split regressions.

Performance impact: The adjacency adaptor adds a small (single-digit percent) CPU overhead in the hot path due to fragment bookkeeping; the router reduces expensive backtracking by steering simple tokens to a lightweight regex fast-path and preserves end-to-end token SLOs. We included an optional heuristic to skip stateful routing under high backpressure.

Operational notes:
- New metrics: constraints.router.mode, constraints.adaptor.fragment_retained, constraints.backend.*.latency.
- Feature flag: constraints.router=stateful (values: off, conservative, aggressive). Conservative aims for correctness with minimal overhead; aggressive prioritizes constraint satisfaction at higher CPU cost.

Rollout plan: feature-gate behind staged config, start with conservative in staging, run a week of telemetry, flip to conservative in a small production cohort, then progressively widen. If any regression, a rollback to legacy is immediate by flipping constraints.router=off.

Related work: references ENG-4821 (reliability incidents caused by split function-calls), ENG-4992 (structured-output eval regressions), and SUP-1372 (support ticket with customer reproducer).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc updated
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration tests + fuzz harness added
- [x] Staging canary executed
- [x] Docs and metrics added

Notes for reviewers: The PR touches several core runtime hot paths; please focus on: correctness of incremental CFG suspension points, deterministic ordering in the priority table, and potential memory growth from retained fragments for long-running requests. I added extensive comments in adaptor.rs for the normalization choices.

release_notes:
Introduces an opt-in stateful constraint router that unifies CFG and regex constraint handling across streaming boundaries, plus a tokenizer adjacency adaptor to prevent structured-output corruption when frames split subtokens. Feature is behind a config flag: constraints.router.

Impact: opt-in; expected to reduce structured-output split regressions in streaming mode.

Operational: new metrics and a conservative rollout plan recommended.
example_diff_snippet:
diff --git a/core/tokenizer/adaptor.rs b/core/tokenizer/adaptor.rs
@@ -12,6 +12,24 @@ pub struct TokenizerAdjacencyAdaptor {
-    // previous implementation: stateless trimming
+    // new: retain partial suffix/prefix per-request and expose a continuation token to constraint engines
+    // we keep at most 2 subtokens of context to avoid unbounded growth; longer sequences fall back to stateless mode
+    retained_suffix: Option<String>,
+    retained_prefix: Option<String>,
+    // TTL measured in emitted-token-count to auto-evict fragments for very long lived requests
+    fragment_ttl: u16,
 }
notes_for_ops: When enabling constraints.router=stateful in Dedicated/Private, monitor constraints.adaptor.fragment_retained and backend latencies. Set conservative mode initially. If fragment_retained grows unbounded for certain customers, flip to off for that tenant and open an investigation. The staging canary config is ci/pipelines/constraint-router-canary.yml.
synthetic_reproducer: Included in runtime/tests/constraint_stream_integration.rs: a harness that takes a golden structured-output (JSON with nested objects and tool-call arguments), tokenizes it with production tokenizer, then slices the token stream into random frame sizes and asserts that the reconstructed streamed output matches the golden structure. The harness includes a replay helper used in the staging canary.
